column1: # WALL-CLOCK ONLY: a stale row can never change a verdict, only cost seconds;
# it also sets each suite's watchdog budget (max(floor, 2 × last)) when no
# verdict row exists, so a row far below a suite's real wall is a kill.
# The scheduler prefers the last full verdict's duration rows (the project
# store's gate/verdict.json "durations"); this file is the cold-start seed
# and the CI shard-bucketing input (scripts/gate/ci-shard.sh — CI has no
# verdict.json). Rows are bare `suite<TAB>seconds` — the scheduler's sed
# accepts nothing else — one per live suite, carrying that suite's last
# POOLED seconds; a suite with no verdict row yet carries its class median
# (listed under the estimate marker below). Unlisted (new) suites default
# to 30 s. Refresh idiom: after a full pool, re-seed every row from
# verdict.json "durations"; a suite rename carries its row to the new name.
# RE-BASELINED from a hosted gate run: measured
# hosted first-attempt walls, with the drive-heavy PTY estates inflated for
# the movie-scaled capture profile (fixed-schedule drives run ~scale× their
# authored seconds on the hosted runner — the local pool at scale 1 is
# unchanged, and a stale row still only costs balance, never a verdict).
